description.en-US: Points at the template-scoped allowed value rather than the global attribute value, so a variant cannot be built from a value its template does not allow.

A copy of the template attribute value's sales_price_extra, held here so the variant can sum it.

A copy is not the preference — it is the only shape that works. The variant's effective_base_sales_price sums this across the variant's chosen values, and that sum has to be a SQL aggregate to avoid a per-row query on every list. An aggregate may only read a real column on a DIRECTLY related schema: the resolver refuses a two-edge source outright, and refuses a computed field with 'it has no column to query'. Reading the template value two hops away is therefore not expressible, and the alternative — a Go-evaluated function field — would run once per row and turn any product listing into N+1.

It is written by the domain service on create and re-propagated when the template value changes; a client may not set it. That is what keeps a copy from becoming a second source of truth. The template attribute value remains authoritative: if the two ever disagree, this one is wrong.
